value.name: counselor urges temporary restraint
value.description: Asha asks the family to give one another the benefit of the doubt for the next two weeks despite not feeling it yet.
evidence: I would like to ask each of you — and I am asking this as a person who has watched many families do this badly and a few do it well — to give each other, for the next two weeks, the benefit of a doubt you do not yet feel like extending.

value.name: counselor ends meeting and leaves
value.description: Asha stands, says she will leave, and tells the family the memorandum is on the table and the appraiser will call that afternoon.
evidence: "I will see myself out," she said. "The memorandum is on the table. The appraiser will call this afternoon to arrange access. Please call my office if anything arises."

value.name: Daniel stops counselor at the door
value.description: As Asha reaches the dining room door, Daniel calls her back by name.
evidence: She walked to the dining room door. She had her hand on the doorframe when Daniel said her name.

value.name: Daniel asks for legal advice
value.description: Daniel stands up and asks Asha to answer him strictly as the estate attorney because he does not know whom else to ask.
evidence: He was standing now. He had pushed his chair back.
"I want to ask you something," he said, "and I want you to answer it as my attorney and not as — not as anything else. Because I don't know who to ask."

value.name: Asha clarifies her role
value.description: Asha tells Daniel she is not his attorney but the estate's attorney, distinguishing her role from personal representation.
evidence: "I am not your attorney, Mr. Serrano. I am the attorney for the estate. There is a difference."

value.name: Daniel insists on estate counsel
value.description: Daniel acknowledges the distinction and presses Asha to answer him in her capacity as estate attorney.
evidence: "I know there is a difference. Answer me as the attorney for the estate."

value.name: Daniel asks whether he needs a lawyer
value.description: Daniel directly asks Asha if he should get his own lawyer, signaling legal anxiety and possible conflict.

value.name: Lucia reacts to legal question
value.description: Lucia makes another small, distinct sound in response to Daniel's question, showing the question affects her too.
evidence: Lucia made another small noise, different from the first.

value.name: Asha weighs her answer carefully
value.description: Asha pauses to consider Daniel's question with great care because her answer could shape the family's next weeks and future relationships.
evidence: Asha considered the question. She considered it with the care it deserved, which was considerable, because the answer would shape the next two weeks and possibly the rest of the family's relationship with itself
